title: Protocol for tridimensional analysis of premaxila and nasopalatine canal using Cone-Beam Computed Tomography
protocol: Place the patient sitting in the i-CAT unit with the head positioned between the beam and the receiver.
Adjust the height of the patient until the chin lies on the chin rest, maintaining an upright posture.
Adjust the headband around the forehead.

Mark the correct position by laser lines projected onto the patient's head: a horizontal line coinciding with the occlusal plane, a vertical line 3.5 cm in front of the condyle, and another vertical line cutting across the sagittal plane of the patient's head.
Perform a preview scan of the patient's head.

Scan the patient’s head using a radiation dose of 120 Kv and 5 mA, with a radiation time of 14.7 seconds, focus-plate distance of 70 cm, resolution of 0.25 or 0.3 voxels, and field of view from 70 to 110 cm.
Reconstruct the scan digitally.
Analyze images using the i-CATVision program in the MPR Screen format.
Simultaneously perform an analysis on axial, sagittal, and coronal anatomical planes.
Arrange all cursors with a cut-off amplitude of 0.25 mm.
Perform linear and angular measurements of NC.
Measure buccal bone plate \(BBP) and palatal bone plate \(PBP) on the three anatomical planes.
Conduct a morphological analysis on the three anatomical planes of NC.
Evaluate images for NC and bone plates measurements.
Make NC, BBP, and PBP measurements at level 1 along the NC.
Locate the axial slice where the incisive foramen of NC is completely closed.
Perform a dynamic vision in the axial slice from the most coronal zone to the nasal cavity.
Visualize the closed NC at the incisive foramen or level 1.
Measure simultaneously in all three anatomical planes \(axial, sagittal, and coronal).
Optimize working time by moving the cursor in the axial plane while cursors in sagittal and coronal planes are automatically adjusted to their respective level 1.
Measure the buccal-palatal diameter \(bpD1) and transversal diameter \(tD1) of NC in an axial slice.
Identify the maximum bpD1 between the buccal and palatal bone cortical of NC.
Determine tD1 as the maximum diameter perpendicular to bpD1.
Measure the BBP widths from BBP buccal wall to NC at three points: left \(LW1), central \(CW1) and right \(RW1).
Establish LW1 between the vestibular cortical of NC left border and the BBP external plate anterior to NC.
Determine CW1 as the width established between the anterior nasal spine and the most anterior and central point of NC.
Identify RW1 as the width from the vestibular cortical of NC right border to the BBP external plate anterior to NC.
Measure NC diameter at level 1 \(CD1) in a coronal slice on the horizontal line.
Take BBP width at level 1 \(BW1), NC sagittal diameter at level 1\(SD1), and PBP width at level 1 \(PW1) in a sagittal slice.
Measure BBP length at level 1\(BL1) from the horizontal line to the inferior edges of BBP.
Measure PBP length at level 1 \(PL1) from the horizontal line to the inferior edges of PBP.
Measure the length of NC (NCL) in the sagittal slice.
Place the red horizontal line at the midpoint of NCL in the sagittal plane.
In the axial slice, measure the buccal-palatal diameter (bpD2) of NC.
Measure the transversal diameter (tD2) of NC in the axial slice.
Measure the BBP width from the vestibular cortical of NC left border to the external plate anterior to NC (LW2).
Measure the BBP width from the anterior nasal spine to the most anterior and central point of NC (CW2).
Measure the BBP width from the vestibular cortical of NC right border to the external plate anterior to NC (RW2).
Take the NC diameter measurement at level 2 in a coronal slice.
In a sagittal slice, measure the BBP width at level 2.
Measure the NC sagittal diameter at level 2 in a sagittal slice.
Measure the PBP width at level 2 in a sagittal slice.
Measure the horizontal distance from the line to the inferior edge of BBP for BL2.
Measure the horizontal distance from the line to the inferior edge of PBP for PL2.
Locate level 3 on the sagittal plane at the foramina of Stenson.
Take the NC diameter measurement at level 3 in a coronal slice.
Take measurements of PBP width at level 3 (PW3) on a sagittal slice.
Measure NC sagittal diameter at level 3 (SD3).
Measure BBP length at level 3 (BL3).
Calculate total BBP length (tBL) by joining midpoints of coronal and apical BBP width.
Draw the LNC in the sagittal plane.
Draw a tangential line to the nasal floor.
Measure the angle formed between the LNC and the tangential line to obtain the nasopalatine angle.
Classify NC morphology in the sagittal plane according to the classification by Mardinger et al.3 and Song et al.18.
Classify NC morphology in the coronal plane following the classification by Bornstein et al.5.
Classify NC morphology in the axial plane based on the classification established by the research team's criteria.
Evaluate all sagittal NC images to establish NC morphology.
Evaluate coronal NC images from anterior to posterior.
Evaluate axial NC images from the incisive foramen to the foramina of Stenson.
Classify NC morphology in sagittal slices according to Mardinger et al.'s protocol.
Identify funnel type NCs with a narrower apical anatomy that widens coronally.
Identify cylindrical type NCs with parallel vestibular and palatal cortices from incisor foramen to the foramina of Stenson.
Identify hourglass type NCs with wide incisor foramen, wide foramina of Stenson, and narrow medial zone.
Evaluate the NC coronal morphology by checking all tomographic slices containing the NC from anterior to posterior.
Classify the NC into three main categories according to the classification by Bornstein et al.: Single, Separate parallels, Y-type.
Subclassify the Y-type category as Ya if two definite branches descend from the foramina of Stenson.
Measure the distance from the cemento-enamel junction to BBP on the buccal surface of teeth 11 and 21.
Measure the distance from the cemento-enamel junction to PBP on the palate surface of teeth 11 and 21.
Calculate the mean value of these measurements for both teeth 11 and 21 to define periodontal condition.
Classify subjects into normal periodontal condition if ≤3 mm.
Classify subjects with moderate periodontitis if >3-≤6 mm.
Classify subjects with severe periodontitis if >6 mm.
